objective: Amount text with a minus sign loses the sign when the amount is smaller than one unit. The text `-0.50` is read as plus 50 cents, so a catalogue row priced -0.50 is accepted as an item costing 0.50, and an order line with unit price -0.25 is accepted as 0.25, although negative prices must be refused. Amount text with a leading minus sign must be read as a negative number of cents (or as zero when the amount is zero), whatever its size. Everything that is read correctly today (positive amounts, negative amounts of 1.00 or more, a leading `$`, thousands separators, surrounding whitespace) must keep its value.
acceptance: Negative amounts between -1 and 0 keep their sign: `-0.50` is -50 cents, `-0.05` is -5, `-0.5` is -50, `-0.99` is -99, `-0.01` is -1, `-0.10` is -10, also with surrounding whitespace
Zero and positive amounts are unchanged: `0.00`, `-0` and `-0.00` are 0, `0.50` is 50, `0.05` is 5, `$0.75` is 75, `12.34` is 1234

For every whole number of cents from -500 to 500, and for -123456, -100000, -99999, -100001 and 123456, reading the text that `format_money(cents, symbol="")` produces gives back the same number of cents
A catalogue file with an item price of `-0.50` or of `-0.05` is refused with a `ParseError`, also when it follows a valid row
An order file with unit price `-0.25` is refused with a `ParseError`, while unit price `0.25` is read as 25 cents
`stockroom items --file F` on a catalogue with an item priced -0.50 returns exit code 1, writes `stockroom: error: ...` to stderr and nothing to stdout
